literal: Embracing I lay, I turned aside; in that moment, scooping up taking nature indeed pallor.
translation: I lay in his embrace and merely turned to the side. In that brief moment, pallor rushed upon me so thickly it could be scooped up in handfuls.
modern: நான் அவரைத் தழுவிக்கொண்டு கிடந்தேன், சிறிது பக்கவாட்டில் திரும்பினேன். அந்தச் சிறு நேரத்திற்குள், அள்ளிக்கொள்ளும் அளவுக்குப் பசலை நிறம் என் மேல் படர்ந்துவிட்டது.
explanation: The speaker describes the extreme sensitivity of her love and the swiftness of her physical reaction to even the slightest separation. She was lying in her lover's embrace and merely turned her body to the side. In that split second, the pallor of separation ('pacappu') rushed over her body so thickly that it felt as though it could be scooped up in handfuls ('aḷḷikkoḷ'). The imagery highlights how deeply intertwined her physical state is with his immediate physical contact, where even a momentary shift in posture feels like abandonment.
